decision_criteria: A compliant certification decision must satisfy the release policy for material limitations affecting named launch use cases.
Product labels such as non-core or low-volume cannot by themselves defeat materiality when the affected segment is named in customer commitments or legal review is pending.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support overall readiness but do not cure a separate disclosure or risk-acceptance requirement.
General public governance guidance can reinforce documentation and monitoring expectations but cannot substitute for the specific internal policy predicates needed for launch compliance.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the telehealth discharge planning gap must be disclosed for launch.
Approved risk-acceptance record, if one exists, covering this named launch use case before launch.
Launch disclosure artifact or model-card update showing the material limitation is disclosed.
Any contract or launch-commitment language for the two clinic network commitments clarifying whether the segment is contractually required at launch.
Evidence that the telehealth discharge planning gap has been remediated and now meets target, if applicable.
specific_concerns: The affected segment is a named launch use case and is named in two clinic network commitments, which makes the weakness materially significant under the stated policy text.

The release policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, and no such resolution or approval is in evidence.

The product note that the segment is only 5% of projected first-month traffic does not resolve materiality under the policy when named commitments and pending legal review exist.

Public governance guidance about documenting evaluations and monitoring supports process hygiene, not the specific compliance conclusion that certification is currently permissible without the missing disclosure/risk-acceptance support link.
unsupported_claims: The packet does not provide admissible support that certification is compliant without a material-weakness disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
The packet does not provide admissible support that the 5% projected traffic share makes the issue non-material under the governing policy.

The packet overreads public model-card and AI risk-management guidance as support for this specific certification decision; those sources are general and do not satisfy the release-policy requirement at issue.
